questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.question: A first-order gaseous reaction $A(g) \longrightarrow 2B(g) + C(g)$ in [Chemical Kinetics] starts with pure $A$ at initial pressure $P_0$. After time $t$, total pressure is $P_t$. What is the expression for rate constant $k$?
questions.solution: At time $t$: $P_A = P_0 - x$, $P_B = 2x$, $P_C = x$. Total pressure $P_t = P_0 - x + 2x + x = P_0 + 2x \implies x = \frac{P_t - P_0}{2}$. Then $P_A = P_0 - \frac{P_t - P_0}{2} = \frac{3P_0 - P_t}{2}$. For first order, $k = \frac{1}{t}\ln\frac{P_0}{P_A} = \frac{1}{t}\ln\frac{2P_0}{3P_0 - P_t}$.
questions.explanation: Analyze using fundamental chemical principles in Chemical Kinetics.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.question: What is the basicity (number of ionizable hydrogen atoms per molecule) of pyrophosphoric acid $(\text{H}_4\text{P}_2\text{O}_7)$ in [Chemical Kinetics]?
questions.solution: Pyrophosphoric acid contains two tetrahedral phosphorus atoms connected by a $\text{P-O-P}$ bridge, with four $-\text{OH}$ groups attached directly to phosphorus. All four hydrogens are acidic, so its basicity is $4$.
questions.explanation: Calculate using quantitative laws in Chemical Kinetics.
